challenges.name: reusable-node-ci
challenges.title: Write the shared Node CI workflow
challenges.description: Rice Rocket's three repositories (app, admin, courier-app) each copied the same CI file, and the copies drifted: one still installs Node 20, one lost its npm cache, one has no time limit. The fix is one reusable workflow in the `rice-rocket/.github` repository that every repository calls with `uses: rice-rocket/.github/.github/workflows/node-ci.yml@v1`. The editor holds `node-ci.yml` with its key blocks missing, each marked by a `# [ ]` line; some pieces are wrong on purpose. Fill every line so that: callers must pass `working-directory` (a string), may pass `node-version` (a string, `24` when omitted) and `run-integration` (a boolean, off when omitted); every command runs in the caller's folder with the caller's Node version and an npm cache keyed on that folder's lockfile; the integration tests run only when the caller sets `run-integration: true`; and the caller can read the line coverage as the workflow output `coverage`, taken from the `cov` step. Run grades the file by calling it the way the three repositories do, with a simulator of GitHub's `workflow_call` inputs, secrets, expressions and outputs.
hints: Follow one value from the caller to its use: `with: { working-directory: api }` must be declared under `on.workflow_call.inputs`, then read where the commands run and where the cache looks for the lockfile. Do the same for `coverage` in the other direction: step, job, workflow.

Look at `inputs.<name>` (not `github.event.inputs`, which belongs to `workflow_dispatch`), at the `type:` and `default:` of each input, at `jobs.<id>.outputs` versus `on.workflow_call.outputs.<name>.value`, and at which contexts each of those may use. Compare how a boolean and the string `'true'` behave in `==`.

A reusable deploy workflow with a typed input and an output: `on: { workflow_call: { inputs: { dry-run: { type: boolean, default: true } }, outputs: { url: { value: "${{ jobs.deploy.outputs.url }}" } } } }`, the job `deploy` with `outputs: { url: "${{ steps.release.outputs.url }}" }`, and a step guarded by `if: ${{ !inputs.dry-run }}`.
